islam-volume-1-number-1-april-1974.description: This inaugural issue of the journal Islam presents a collection of scholarly articles and devotional excerpts intended to articulate an Islamic perspective on theology, history, and scripture. The contributors examine the historical and spiritual foundations of the faith, with a particular focus on the Qur’an as the ultimate reference for all religious inquiry. The volume includes an analysis of biblical prophecies concerning Muhammad, a defense against historical claims regarding the spread of Islam by force, and a discussion on the compatibility of Christian beliefs with Qur’anic teachings. Furthermore, the journal features linguistic commentary on the Qur’an, explorations of Sufi aphorisms and invocations, and a series of chronological conversion tables for the Islamic calendar. Throughout the text, the authors emphasize the unity of religious belief and the necessity of maintaining piety, while critiquing external interpretations of Islamic history and social practices.

toc.title: Islam: Its Mission in the World 1. Unity of Religious Belief

salat-booklet.description: Rashad Khalifa presents a guide to the daily Contact Prayers, or Salat, arguing that these practices originate from the religion of Abraham as established in the Quran. He asserts that modern Islamic traditions have deviated from the original divine instructions and seeks to restore the correct methodology through a step-by-step manual. The text details the necessary preparations, including the Azaan and the ritual ablution, before outlining the physical movements and recitations required for each prayer unit. Khalifa emphasizes the importance of the opening chapter of the Quran, known as The Key, as a unifying recitation for all believers. The work further explains the variations in prayer units for different times of the day, the protocols for group and congregational worship, and the specific requirements for the Friday prayer.

toc.title: Preparation for the Contact Prayer (The Ablution)
HOW TO PERFORM THE CONTACT PRAYERS

computer-speaks.description: This work presents a series of mathematical analyses of the Quran, which the author argues provide physical, verifiable evidence of a divine code based on the number 19. He asserts that this numerical pattern confirms the Quran as a perfectly preserved message from God and serves as a proof of its authenticity. The text is organized into a series of "physical facts," each detailing specific counts of alphabet letters, words, and chapter structures that align with multiples of 19. He presents these findings to demonstrate that the Quranic initials—mysterious letters prefixed to certain chapters—are not merely ornamental but are integral to a complex, divinely orchestrated system. The author further discusses the historical implications of these findings, including his calculations regarding the end of the world, and provides extensive appendices that address theological topics such as the nature of God, the role of the Prophet, and the relationship between the Quran and previous scriptures.

toc.title: CONCLUSION AND COMMENTS ON PHYSICAL FACTS 9, 10, 11, & 12
LIST OF THE ARABIC ALPHABETS AND THEIR NUMERICAL VALUES

english-meanings-of-the-quran.description: This text provides an English translation and theological commentary on selected portions of the Quran, specifically focusing on Sura Al-Fatihah and the opening verses of Sura Al-Baqarah. The author, Rashad Khalifa, presents his work as the first English rendering of the Quranic meanings by a Muslim Arab, intended to clarify fundamental Islamic principles for a contemporary audience. He argues that the Quran possesses a unique linguistic efficiency and a mathematical structure that serves as evidence of its divine origin. Through a combination of verse-by-verse translation and analytical commentary, he explores themes such as the nature of God, the necessity of belief in the hereafter, and the importance of daily prayer. The author further incorporates findings from computerized studies of the text, claiming that the frequency of specific letters and the arrangement of suras demonstrate a divinely ordained system that transcends human capability.

eternity-screenplay.description: This screenplay by Dr. Rashad Khalifa explores a complex narrative spanning human history, theology, and science fiction. The plot begins in 1985 with the discovery of a time capsule containing a mathematical code, which leads to the identification of a lost will belonging to a pioneer named Barclay Leland Stamford. As the narrative progresses, the focus shifts to a futuristic space odyssey aboard the spacecraft Eternity, commanded by Virgil Moss. The crew, accompanied by advanced robots, travels through hyperspace and encounters celestial entities, including angels and Satan. The author presents a theological framework in which he argues that God created seven universes and that humanity is undergoing a probationary test on Earth. The screenplay interweaves these cosmic events with scenes of human suffering, religious conflict, and political tension on Earth, ultimately suggesting a struggle between divine protection and satanic influence.

hard-cover-1989.description: This work presents an authorized English translation of the Quran, accompanied by the original Arabic text. The author, Dr. Rashad Khalifa, argues that the Quran is a divinely guarded message characterized by a perpetual mathematical miracle based on the number 19. He presents the text as a final testament intended to consolidate and purify all previous divine messages, asserting that Islam is a description of total submission to God alone rather than a sectarian name. The volume is organized into 114 suras, each preceded by its name, verse count, and page location. Following the translated text, the author provides extensive appendices that detail his mathematical findings, which he claims authenticate the Quran's structure and expose human-authored distortions in traditional interpretations. He emphasizes that the Quran is fully detailed and sufficient for salvation, rejecting the authority of traditional Hadith and Sunna.

islam-volume-1-number-2-july-1974.description: This issue of the journal Islam serves as an international platform for theological discourse, focusing on the preservation and interpretation of the Qur'an. The publication features articles that examine the mission of Islam in the modern world, emphasizing the necessity of reconciling religious sentiment with reason. Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents a series of mathematical analyses of the Qur'anic initials, arguing that these patterns provide empirical evidence of the text's divine preservation. Other contributors explore the Islamic perspective on racial equality, the historical origins of Islamic jurisprudence, and the spiritual insights found in Sufi aphorisms and invocations. The volume also includes a translation of the second chapter of the Qur'an, a guide to the Islamic calendar, and a critical review of contemporary apocalyptic literature, all presented within the framework of promoting a unified understanding of God's message to humanity.

toc.title: Islam: Its Mission in the World
Islamic Concentrates: The Aphorisms of Salamah Al-Radi

islam-volume-1-number-3-4-january-1975.description: This issue of the journal ISLAM serves as a platform for diverse scholarly and theological contributions aimed at articulating an Islamic perspective on contemporary and historical issues. The volume is organized into a series of thematic articles, followed by a section titled Islamic Concentrates, which offers aphorisms, invocations, and reference tools. Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents arguments regarding the mathematical design of the Qur'an, while other contributors examine the historical authenticity of the Gospel of Barnabas, the status of Jerusalem in Islamic thought, and the political implications of the Third International Theory. The volume also includes a critical analysis of the falsification of Hadith, in which Muhammad 'Ajjaj Al-Khatib argues that political and sectarian divisions historically motivated the fabrication of traditions. The journal concludes with educational resources, including an index to the Qur'an and a calendar conversion table, intended to support the study of Islamic texts.

toc.title: Propagation of Islam: The Basic Principles
Islam: Its Mission in the World
Islamic Concentrates: The Aphorisms of Salamah Al-Radi

miracle-of-quran-alphabets.description: This study investigates the significance of the mysterious alphabets, or Qur'anic initials, that prefix twenty-nine chapters of the Qur'an. The author presents a mathematical analysis of these letters, arguing that their frequency and distribution within the text demonstrate a divine, non-human origin for the scripture. He details a four-year research project utilizing computer-aided calculations to determine the absolute frequency, percentage, and per-verse occurrence of these initials across all 114 suras. The work is organized by specific initial sets, with each chapter dedicated to the statistical results of a particular letter or combination, such as Qaf, Nun, Sad, and various multi-letter groupings. He presents evidence suggesting that these initials correlate with the chronological and recorded sequences of the suras, asserting that the mathematical balance observed is beyond the capacity of any human author. The text concludes by framing these findings as a perpetual, verifiable miracle intended to provide scientific reassurance to believers and skeptics alike.

quran-hadith-islam.description: This work presents a theological argument for the doctrine of Quran-alone Islam, asserting that the Quran is the complete, perfect, and sole source of religious guidance for Muslims. The author contends that the reliance on Hadith and Sunna—traditions attributed to the Prophet Muhammad—constitutes a form of idolatry and a direct violation of divine commandments. He argues that Muhammad was strictly forbidden from uttering any religious instructions outside of the Quranic revelation and that the prophet's role was limited to the delivery of the scripture. The text is organized into short, thematic sections that combine Quranic citations with the author's commentary, emphasizing that historical religious practices, such as Salat and Hajj, were established through Abraham rather than through the later traditions of Hadith. The author further presents numerical evidence based on the number 19 to support his claims regarding the Quran's divine preservation and structural integrity, ultimately calling for a return to monotheistic worship centered exclusively on the Quran.

quran1981.description: This translation of the Quran, authored by Dr. Rashad Khalifa, presents an authorized English version of the scripture intended to provide a clear and direct understanding of the divine message. The work is organized into 114 suras, each containing verses that the author presents as the infallible word of God. Khalifa argues that the Quran is a divinely guarded scripture and he emphasizes its role as the final message to humanity, intended to guide individuals toward salvation through submission to God alone. He presents a detailed numerical analysis, which he claims serves as a physical, indisputable proof of the Quran's divine origin, and he argues that this miraculous code remained hidden for 1400 years. The text includes extensive appendices that address theological topics such as the nature of God, the role of the prophet, and the history of previous scriptures, while also providing a genealogical table and indices to assist the reader in navigating the content.

perpetual-miracle.description: This text presents a theological argument for the divine origin of the Qur'an based on a mathematical system centered on the number 19. The author posits that the Qur'an contains a perpetual miracle, manifested through a complex numerical structure that remains consistent across the entire text. He argues that the basmala, the opening verse of the Qur'an, serves as the key to this system, as its letter count and the frequency of its constituent words throughout the scripture are multiples of 19. He further contends that this mathematical design extends to the mysterious initials found at the beginning of certain suras, suggesting that their specific distribution and frequency provide empirical, verifiable proof of the text's preservation and authorship by God. The author asserts that these findings are physical facts, independent of linguistic interpretation, and intended for all of humanity.

quran-visual-presentation.description: This work presents a mathematical analysis of the Quran, arguing that a hidden numerical code based on the number 19 serves as physical evidence of its divine origin. The author contends that this secret remained concealed for 1,400 years until its unveiling through modern computation. He presents a series of fifty-two physical facts, detailing how the frequency of specific letters, words, and verse counts across various chapters consistently align with multiples of 19. He argues that this pattern extends to the Quranic initials, the opening statement, and the distribution of divine names. The text is organized as a catalog of these mathematical observations, providing lists of chapter and verse occurrences to support his claims regarding the structural integrity and miraculous nature of the scripture.
